versions.short: The bill would expand support for maternity care in rural areas that lack specialty maternity care or dedicated obstetric units, so that local providers could better handle prenatal, labor, birthing, and postpartum care during emergencies, including through telehealth and regional partnerships. It would direct the Secretary to award grants of at least $2,000,000 per fiscal year for these activities, to develop obstetric readiness programs and training, and to fund evidence-based best practices. It would also require a report every two years, starting in 2028, that includes a study of maternity ward closures and patient transport patterns. Finally, it would extend funding authorizations for telehealth networks and related health programs through fiscal years 2027 to 2031.
